topic: Snyk Evo Agentic Development Security (ADS) Review 2026
summary: Snyk Evo ADS is a new security product launched June 23, 2026 (GA June 29) that provides real-time governance for AI coding agents. It secures what agents use (supply chain), what they do (behavior), and what they generate (output) — operating inside the agent execution loop rather than downstream. Part of Snyk's Evo product line alongside AI-SPM (GA March 2026) and Continuous Offensive Security, forming the 'AI Security Fabric'. The launch was timed to the AI Engineer World's Fair where Snyk was the exclusive security sponsor. Evo ADS is the third pillar of Snyk's AI Security Platform, now covering the full software lifecycle: from agents writing code (ADS) to models running in production (AI-SPM) to applications the agents build (COS).

secure_agent_supply_chain.description: Discovers and assesses MCP servers, skills, and external tools agents pull in — before agents interact with them
capabilities: Surfaces prompt injection in agent toolchains
Detects malicious code patterns in skills/plugins
Assesses supply chain risks before agents interact with tools
Creates policies to flag risky components with severity
Vets MCP servers for malicious configurations and backdoors

govern_agent_behavior.description: Monitors and enforces real-time policy on agent actions during execution — inside the agent workflow
capabilities: Governs systems agents access and workflows they run
Detects prompt injection, agent hijacking, secret exfiltration
Full session and intent context for policy decisions

ensure_trusted_output.description: Scans and fixes AI-generated vulnerabilities at the moment of creation — security at inception
capabilities: Fixes before code is suggested to developer
Works inside Claude, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, Windsurf
Real-time vulnerability scanning of AI-generated code
Enforces security at inception rather than in post-production review

Part of unified AI Security Fabric (code + agents + production AI apps)
First-to-market in the 'Agentic Development Security' category

key_people.manoj_nair: Chief Technology & Innovation Officer, Snyk — 'Ask a security leader for a complete inventory of the AI agents, MCP servers, and skills running across their developer machines — in most organizations, that inventory doesn't exist. That is the gap Evo ADS closes.'
key_people.brendan_putek: Director of DevOps, Relay Network (early customer) — engineering teams run GitHub Copilot, Codex, and Windsurf, moving to Claude Code as primary coding assistant

market_positioning: Snyk positions Evo ADS as the enforcement layer for AI agents building enterprise software. It addresses the gap where existing security tools scan code after writing but have no visibility into MCP configurations, skills, or agent runtime behavior. The product targets CISOs, security engineers, and engineering leaders adopting AI coding agents. Snyk pitches the launch as a response to a gap that conventional security tooling was never designed to cover — AI coding assistants have turned into autonomous agents that call external tools, take actions, and connect to internal systems through MCP servers, skills, and plugins, creating an entirely new attack surface.
key_risks_addressed: Malicious MCP servers compromising agent toolchains
Prompt injection embedded in agent dependencies
Supply chain attacks via compromised skills/plugins
Lack of inventory/visibility into AI agents, MCP servers, and skills across developer machines
verdict: Snyk Evo ADS represents a new category (Agentic Development Security) that addresses a genuine and growing gap in AI security governance. Its key strength is operating inside the agent execution loop rather than post-hoc scanning — real-time enforcement of what agents use, do, and generate. The product is backed by substantial telemetry (9,700 environments) and documented real-world attack scenarios. The main risks: (1) it requires deep integration with multiple rapidly-evolving AI coding platforms (Claude, Copilot, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf) and the MCP ecosystem; (2) the category is nascent and enterprise adoption patterns are unproven; (3) competitors (Wiz, GitHub, Veracode) are likely to enter this space. GA as of June 29, 2026 makes it very early-stage but first-to-market in this specific category. The broader Snyk AI Security Platform strategy (AI-SPM + COS + ADS) is coherent and defensible as a unified 'AI Security Fabric' for the full software lifecycle.
